hero.h1: Pre-purchase property inspection in Dublin and Meath
hero.sub: A practical inspection of a second-hand home by construction people, before you sign. You get a written report on what we found and what needs a closer look.

intro.title: Know what you are buying
paragraphs: A second-hand home can hide damp, tired windows or a roof that needs work. Our pre-purchase property inspection looks at the visible condition of the house and tells you, in plain English, what we found.
Wanessa leads our property inspection service and is your contact from booking to report.

included.title: What the inspection covers
items: General condition of the house, inside and out
Roof: visible condition from the ground, and the roof space where safely accessible
Attic insulation and ventilation, where accessible
Walls, floors and ceilings: visible cracks, movement and defects
Visible signs of damp and moisture
External walls, render, brickwork, gutters and downpipes
Services: a visual look at the electrics, plumbing and heating
Extensions and alterations worth a closer look
A written report of significant defects and recommended next steps

price.headline: €650 plus VAT
price.note: For a pre-purchase property inspection of a second-hand home. An optional repair and upgrade estimate is available on request.

process.title: Book
process.text: Send us the address and where you are in the sale by WhatsApp, phone or the form.

process.title: Inspection
process.text: We inspect the visible condition of the house, including the attic if it is accessible.

process.title: Written report
process.text: You receive a clear report of what we found, with anything that needs an engineer or specialist flagged.

process.title: Estimate, if you want one
process.text: On request, we price the repairs and upgrades you are considering.

faqs.a: Before you sign. The report is most useful while you can still ask questions or negotiate.

faqs.q: Do you test the heating and electrics?
faqs.a: Services are checked visually. We do not test services unless that has been agreed in advance.

faqs.q: Can you tell me what repairs will cost?
faqs.a: Yes. On request, we add an estimate for repairs and upgrades to the report.
Wanessa leads the property inspection service and is your contact from booking to report.

No. It is a visual, non-invasive pre-purchase inspection by construction people. It does not include structural calculations or an engineer's report. Where something needs an engineer, the report says so.

faqs.q: Do you check planning and Building Regulations compliance?
faqs.a: No. Compliance and title documents are a matter for your solicitor. We point out extensions or alterations that look worth asking about.

sections.title: How the inspection works
paragraphs: It is a visual, non-invasive inspection of what can be seen and safely reached on the day. We do not lift floor coverings, move furniture or open up walls, floors or finishes.
Where something needs a structural engineer, an electrician or another specialist, the report says so plainly, so you can arrange that before you commit.

sections.title: What it does not include
bullets: Structural calculations or a structural engineer's report
Testing or certification of electrics, gas, plumbing or heating
Planning or Building Regulations compliance checks (your solicitor deals with these)
Anything hidden behind finishes, furniture or stored belongings

sections.title: Other types of survey
paragraphs: The Society of Chartered Surveyors Ireland describes several levels of residential survey, from a general condition report to a more detailed building survey. All of them are visual. If our report suggests you need a more detailed survey or an engineer, we will tell you.
